story.title: Six Nigerians to be Extradited to the US for Alleged Romance Scams
story.summary: Six Nigerian nationals are set to be extradited to the United States to face charges related to an online romance scam that allegedly defrauded American women of over $6 million. The charges include wire fraud and money laundering, according to South African police.

explore_lenses.label: How did the case reach extradition?
explore_lenses.title: A five-year cross-border case
explore_lenses.summary: The extradition follows U.S. indictments and South African arrests in 2021, after a lengthy South African extradition process. The current reporting says six men are being transferred, while the original U.S. case involved eight charged people and seven arrests in South Africa.

claims.text: The U.S. Attorney’s Office for New Jersey announced charges in October 2021 against seven alleged Cape Town-zone Black Axe leaders and an eighth alleged co-conspirator; seven defendants had then been arrested in South Africa.
The Justice Department’s case page says a South African judge denied bail to the arrested defendants in December 2021 and that an extradition trial was scheduled for January 28, 2022.
South African police said the six would be moved from a Cape Town correctional facility to the airport and handed to FBI and U.S. Secret Service officials on September 11, 2026.

explore_lenses.label: Why is this more than a romance-scam case?
explore_lenses.title: Alleged fraud network and money trail
explore_lenses.summary: Prosecutors describe the case as a transnational fraud-and-money-laundering prosecution, not solely a set of false dating profiles. The allegations include use of aliases, U.S.-based accounts and South African businesses to obtain and move proceeds.

claims.text: According to the 2021 U.S. charging announcement, the alleged schemes ran from Cape Town between 2011 and 2021 and used dating and social-media sites, internet-phone numbers and aliases to reach U.S. victims.

Prosecutors allege that proceeds from romance and advance-fee scams, as well as business-email-compromise schemes, were moved to South Africa through victim or other U.S.-based accounts and concealed through business entities.

INTERPOL said the 2021 arrests in Cape Town and Johannesburg were part of international efforts against Black Axe and related networks, illustrating the reliance on cooperation among South African, U.S. and INTERPOL-linked investigators.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the transfer to the U.S.?
explore_lenses.title: Federal charges, not a verdict
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate consequence of a completed extradition would be that the defendants can be brought before the U.S. federal court handling the cases in New Jersey. Any trial, plea agreement, sentence or restitution order would remain unresolved.

claims.text: The original cases were assigned to U.S. District Judge Michael A. Shipp in Trenton federal court, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.
The cited U.S. charges include wire-fraud conspiracy and money-laundering conspiracy; some defendants were also charged with substantive wire fraud and aggravated identity theft.

The Justice Department says wire-fraud and money-laundering counts can each carry maximum prison terms of 20 years, while aggravated identity theft carries a mandatory consecutive two-year term; actual outcomes depend on charges proved, pleas, sentencing rules and judicial decisions.

story_report.summary: Six Nigerian nationals accused of running online romance scams that allegedly defrauded American women of more than $6 million were scheduled to be extradited from South Africa to the United States on Friday, September 11, 2026. South African police said the men would be transferred from a Cape Town correctional facility to an airport and handed over to FBI and U.S. Secret Service officials. They are expected to face U.S. allegations including wire fraud and money laundering, though the available reporting did not confirm that the handover had been completed.

sections.heading: Alleged Cape Town scam operation
sections.body: According to the 2021 U.S. charging announcement, the alleged schemes operated from Cape Town between 2011 and 2021. Prosecutors say the network used dating and social-media platforms, internet-phone numbers and aliases to target U.S. victims. They further allege that money from romance, advance-fee and business-email-compromise scams was routed to South Africa through victim or other U.S.-based accounts, then concealed through business entities.

sections.heading: United States charges and court process
sections.body: The U.S. Attorney’s Office announced charges in October 2021 against seven alleged Cape Town-area Black Axe leaders and an eighth alleged co-conspirator; seven defendants had then been arrested in South Africa. The cases were assigned to U.S. District Judge Michael A. Shipp in Trenton. The cited charges include wire-fraud conspiracy and money-laundering conspiracy, with some defendants also charged with substantive wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. The allegations have not established the defendants’ guilt.

unresolved.text: The supplied reporting does not identify the six people scheduled for transfer or explain why six are now involved when seven defendants were arrested in South Africa in 2021.
The consulted reporting described the September 11 handover as scheduled, without confirming its completion or providing dates for initial U.S. court hearings.

related_stories.title: Ferry Fire in the Philippines Leaves Five Dead and Dozens Missing
related_stories.summary: A fire on a passenger ferry near Coron in the Philippines has resulted in at least five fatalities and left 87 individuals missing. Coast guard crews are conducting searches in challenging sea conditions, with reports indicating that over 40 people have been rescued. The incident occurred near a popular tourist destination in the province of Palawan.

related_stories.title: Commemorating the 25th Anniversary of the September 11 Attacks
related_stories.summary: On the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, ceremonies were held across the United States to honor the nearly 3,000 victims. President Donald Trump attended a ceremony at the Pentagon, while Vice President JD Vance and four former presidents participated in commemorations at Ground Zero in New York. The day was marked by a somber mood as families of victims read the names of those lost in the attacks.

related_stories.title: Fire in Bukavu Claims Lives of Schoolchildren and Destroys Neighborhood
related_stories.summary: A devastating fire in the Kadutu district of Bukavu, Democratic Republic of Congo, has resulted in the deaths of at least 24 schoolchildren. The blaze engulfed two schools and destroyed over 300 homes, leading to a chaotic stampede as people attempted to escape the flames.

related_stories.title: Brother of NYPD Officer Who Died from 9/11-Related Cancer Advocates for Victims
related_stories.summary: As the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks approaches, Phil Alvarez, a retired NYPD detective, reflects on his brother Luis's death from cancer linked to toxins at Ground Zero. Alvarez is working to extend the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund to assist others affected by similar health issues. This year, a seventh moment of silence will be observed to honor those who have died from illnesses related to the toxic dust from the attacks.
